title: Introduce staged sequence-length-aware batch composer with weighted padding cost
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a new staged, sequence-length-aware batch composer that reduces padding-induced token waste. Improves latency/cost tradeoffs for mixed seqlen workloads; default is opt-in behind `staged_batcher.enabled` flag.
description: Context: In production customers are seeing large token waste when short and long requests are mixed. Prior work (seqlen bucketing and percentiles) reduced this but still leaves edge cases where a single long request blocks throughput or short requests incur excessive padding. This PR introduces a staged batch composer: it composes batches in two phases to minimize padding while respecting latency SLOs and kernel-friendly batch sizes. Design highlights: 1) Stage 1 groups requests into coarse seqlen buckets using configurable percentile boundaries derived from sliding-window histograms. 2) Stage 2 composes final batches within each bucket by solving a small knapsack-like composition that optimizes a weighted cost = padding_tokens * padding_weight + wait_time_ms * latency_weight + kv_miss_penalty * kv_weight. This cost formulation lets operators trade a few ms of latency for significant token savings. 3) Kernel awareness: the composer prefers batch sizes that match high-throughput kernels for the active model (for example 8/16/32 depending on model type and quantization); a kernel-profile cache is consulted during composition. 4) KV-cache affinity: requests that share recent KV prefixes are co-located when possible to reuse GPU-side KV rows; the batcher consults a lightweight KV-hotset estimator to reduce KV cache misses. 5) Continuous batching integration: composer plugs into the existing continuous-batching queue with minimal API changes (new BatchComposer interface + factory hook) so runtime scheduling and autoscaling remain unchanged. Motivation & tradeoffs: The staged approach reduces padding by up to 28% on multimodal seqlen traces (see benchmarks), but adds a small CPU overhead for the knapsack solve. We mitigate this with a capped solver budget and a fast greedy fallback. Operators can tune percentiles, solver budget, and weight multipliers. Benchmark summary (representative): - Mixed seqlen e-commerce workload (p50=128, p95=1536): token cost reduced 22%, median latency +3ms, p99 latency unchanged. - Chat-like short requests (p50=48, p95=256): token cost reduced 12%, median latency neutral. - Synthetic stress with interleaved very long sequences: tail latency improved by 9% due to kernel-aware batching avoiding pathological batch compositions. Key files changed (high level): runtime/batching/staged_batcher.cpp/h, runtime/batching/batcher_factory.cpp, runtime/scheduler/slice_scheduler.cpp (hook for kernel profiles), runtime/kv_cache/cache_prefetcher.cpp (hotset estimator), tests/batching/test_staged_batcher.py, docs/ops/batching.md, benchmarks/seqlen_staged/README.md, ci/jenkins/pipeline.yml. Commits: see commit list below for incremental design and tests. Backwards compatibility: gated behind `staged_batcher.enabled=false` by default; config schema extended but old fields are preserved. Rollout plan: opt-in for Dedicated and Private initially, A/B test for hosted API routes with low SLO sensitivity, monitor token-cost and p99 latency. Notes on kernel integration: composer queries a runtime-exposed kernel_profile map (model->preferred batch sizes) and penalizes batches that would produce non-ideal kernel volume; this favors kernels that achieve better amortized launch cost. KV affinity model: lightweight counting Bloom filters per worker summarize recent prefixes — we use them only as heuristics and never as correctness signals. Observability: new metrics added: staged_batch_compositions_total, staged_batch_padding_saved_tokens, staged_batch_solver_time_ms_bucket, staged_batch_kv_affinity_hits. Config knobs: percentiles: [50,90,99], padding_weight: 1.0, latency_weight: 0.1, kv_weight: 2.0, solver_budget_ms: 2, enable_kernel_hinting: true. Benchmarks included in PR under benchmarks/seqlen_staged/ with scripts to reproduce. CI: full unit tests + bench regression check passed. Migration: no data migrations required.

review_comments: Connor Liu: Please add a fast-path no-op when percentiles show a single dominant bucket to avoid extra CPU work. (resolved)
Marta Ivanova: Need explicit limits for solver budget and a clear fallback — the current greedy fallback looks good but add a unit test for its correctness under budget pressure. (addressed)

Samir Rao: How does this interact with existing prefix cache eviction heuristics? Could affinity cause hotspotting on KV cache? Suggest adding a mitigation metric. (added staged_batch_kv_affinity_hits metric)
Connor Liu: CI flaky test on slice_scheduler timeout — reran, fixed race by adding a short spinwait in test harness. (fixed)
Author (Aisha): responded to all comments, kept staged_batcher disabled by default, added docs and a troubleshooting section
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature gated, tunable, and with an inexpensive greedy fallback to avoid CPU tail variance.
Operators should run the provided bench scripts against their request traces before enabling in high-SLA production routes.
Follow-up work tracked in ENG-4823: adaptive percentile learning and model-specific kernel profiles per-quantization-scheme.
